To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the achievable sensitivity of a VIR GO pair to relic gravitational waves of cosmological origin can be significantly improved by a reduction of the thermal noise; 2) in the case of the string cosmology scenario the sensitivity of a VIR-GO pair is expected to be better than that of the LIGO interferometer(s).

a pair of VIRGOS will be able to detect relic gravitational waves in the frequency range 10-10^3 Hz, with a signal-to-noise threshold of order 5-6, for models of the string cosmological scenario with a long dilaton domination, and that a significant reduction of the thermal noise is required to improve the sensitivity of a VIRGOS pair.

(1) a second VIRGO detector would be able to improve the current limits on stochastic backgrounds of cosmological gravitational waves, and (2) the achievable sensitivities depend on the details of the model under investigation.

a pair of VIRGOS, with the thermal noise reduced to the level of the current shot noise, could be able to probe a wide class of string cosmological models.
the sensitivity achievable by a VIRGO pair to stochastic and isotopic gravitational wave background is not yet competitive with that achievable by LIGO.

a VIRGO pair is not expected to provide a competitive sensitivity to relic graviton backgrounds, but that it will be a valuable tool to test the validity of the theoretical models and the consistency of the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in spite of the fact that the sensitivity to relic gravitons is not improved by the reduction of the shot-noise power spectral density (in the case of a VIRGO interferometer pair), a substantial reduction of the thermal noise would allow to improve significantly the expected sensitivity to a class of models (e.g. string cosmological scenarios) where the signal to noise ratio is maximized for small values of the slope of the energy spectrum.

the expected sensitivities achievable by a pair (or a network) of upgraded VIRGO detectors to a stochastic gravitational background of cosmological origin are promising, but the expected sensitivities are not yet competitive with the best results achievable with the LIGO interferometers.
the expected sensitivity of the VIRGO pair is comparable to the one of a single LIGO detector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expected sensitivities of a VIRGO detector pair are comparable with those of LIGO and LISA.

the sensitivity of a pair of VIRGOS is comparable with that of the LISA mission and that the sensitivity to relic gravitons is not significantly affected by a possible non-monotonicity of the logarithmic energy spectrum.
the sensitivity to stochastic backgrounds achievable by a pair VIRGO interferometers is not competitive with that achievable by the two LIGO interferometers.
